paragraphs: Children in care in Hertfordshire are looked after by Hertfordshire County Council's fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council's teenage fostering campaign says 975 children are in its care and that two in three of them (67%) are aged 11 to 17, so carers for teenagers are especially needed. Hertfordshire is part of Foster East, a network of 11 councils across the East of England, where more than 7,000 children are in care at any one time.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21, in good general health and have at least one spare room. You do not need parenting experience, you can have children of your own, and depending on the type of fostering and the child's needs you may be able to keep working.

Carers receive a weekly payment for their skills and a weekly allowance for each child, along with mileage, a set-up payment for furniture and equipment, holiday, birthday and festive allowances, an initial clothing and uniform allowance and local discounts. The council's recruitment pages quote slightly different top rates for the child allowance, so ask the fostering team for the current figures.

Support includes preparation training before you start, core courses such as first aid and safeguarding (mostly held in Stevenage or Apsley, near Hemel Hempstead), a social worker who supervises you monthly, an experienced foster carer as a buddy, local support groups, and an out-of-hours line seven days a week. Carers also get membership of The Fostering Network, and specialist training is offered for fostering teenagers.
If you live in Hertfordshire, speak to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and compare what each offers before you decide.

sources.title: Why foster with us (Hertfordshire County Council)
